questions.q: What syntax does Airflow's `schedule` parameter accept?
options: An Airflow-only proprietary scheduling format
Real cron syntax, the same as Unix crontab
Only the readable presets like @daily — no custom strings allowed
Plain English sentences describing the schedule
questions.explain: Airflow's schedule parameter uses standard cron syntax, not a custom dialect.

questions.q: What is a DAG run's 'logical date'?
options: The exact timestamp the run started executing
The date the DAG file was first created
The start of the period the run represents, not the moment it actually executes
A random identifier with no relationship to time
questions.explain: The logical date represents the period covered by the run, which is often earlier than when the run actually executes.

questions.q: Why is `{{ ds }}` useful in a bash_command, according to this lesson?
options: It always equals the current server time
It gives you the period the run represents, which is what a data pipeline actually needs, not 'right now'
It only works inside PythonOperator, never BashOperator
It has no practical use in real pipelines
questions.explain: ds resolves to the logical date, which correctly represents the data period being processed — not the literal moment of execution.

questions.q: What does `catchup=True` (the default) do for a DAG deployed with a past start_date?
options: Deletes all runs older than a week automatically
Only affects DAGs scheduled hourly
Schedules every missed run between the start date and now, not just future ones
Prevents the DAG from ever running
questions.explain: With catchup=True, Airflow backfills every scheduled run since start_date, which is often not what you want for a 'latest data only' pipeline.

questions.q: Why might you use a real cron string instead of a preset like @daily?
options: When you need something more specific, like '6 AM, weekdays only,' which has no preset equivalent
Presets are always slower to execute than cron strings
Presets don't actually work in current Airflow versions
Cron strings are required for every DAG regardless of need
questions.explain: Presets only cover simple common cases — anything more specific, like weekday-only schedules, requires a real cron expression.
